belongs_to: Figure it Out (third set) Q10: "A tiny park is coming up in Dhauli. The plan is shown in the figure. The two square plots, each of area g^2 sq. ft., will have a green cover ... walking path w ft. wide ... Write an expression for the area that needs to be tiled." (printed pdf page 10, right of the question text)
description: Plan of a rectangular park, drawn on squared-paper texture. One outer rectangle, about twice as wide as tall (roughly 2.0 : 1), with a thick dark outline. The whole rectangle is filled khaki-yellow (olive yellow) and covered by thin grey-blue grid lines (a squared-paper background, about 13 vertical and 7 horizontal lines; the grid is only background texture and is not tied to w or g). Inside it, two identical solid green squares (no grid lines over them, thin dark outline), side by side on the same horizontal level, left square and right square. Each square is about 2.5 times as wide as the khaki margin strip around it. The left square sits at the left, the right square at the right, so the khaki path is: a strip of width w above both squares, a strip of width w below both squares, a strip of width w at the far left, a strip of width w at the far right, and a wider khaki gap between the two squares (about twice w in the drawing; by the printed answer it is 2w). Labels: inside each green square, centred, the text 'g^2 sq. ft.' (italic g with superscript 2). Dimension arrows (all double-headed, thin dark, open arrowheads), 5 in total: (1) TOP: one vertical double-headed arrow in the top khaki strip, between the top edge of the rectangle and the top edge of the left square, roughly above the middle of the left square; the text 'w ft.' (italic w) is printed just to the LEFT of this arrow. (2) BOTTOM: one vertical double-headed arrow in the bottom khaki strip, between the bottom edge of the right square and the bottom edge of the rectangle, roughly below the middle of the right square; the text 'w ft.' is printed just to the LEFT of this arrow. (3) LEFT: one horizontal double-headed arrow in the left khaki strip, between the left edge of the rectangle and the left edge of the left square, placed in the lower part of the left square's height (about 70 percent of the way down the rectangle); NO label printed. (4) MIDDLE: one horizontal double-headed arrow in the gap between the two squares, from the right edge of the left square to the left edge of the right square, at about the middle height; NO label printed. (5) RIGHT: one horizontal double-headed arrow in the right khaki strip, between the right edge of the right square and the right edge of the rectangle, placed in the upper part of the square's height (about 37 percent of the way down the rectangle); NO label printed. So only two arrows carry a printed label (both 'w ft.'); the left, middle and right horizontal arrows are unlabelled (by the printed answer they stand for w, 2w and w). Printed answer on the same page (text only, no picture): length = w+g+2w+g+w = (2g+4w) ft, breadth = w+w+g = (g+2w) ft, area to be tiled = (2g+4w)(g+2w) - 2g^2 = 8w(w+g) sq. ft.
unclear: Exact number of background grid lines (about 13 vertical x 7 horizontal); the grid is a squared-paper texture not aligned with w, g or the squares' edges.
Exact colours are read from the page picture (khaki about #D9CF6E, green about #62BC7E, grid grey-blue); the picture carries a faint 'NCERT not to be republished' watermark across it.

Exact drawn proportions are approximate: outer rectangle about 269 x 134 px, squares about 75 x 75 px, side/top/bottom margins about 29 px, gap between squares about 61 px on the 981 px-wide page picture.

belongs_to: Figure it Out (third set) Q11 pattern (a): "For each pattern shown below, (i) Draw the next figure in the sequence. (ii) How many basic units are there in Step 10? (iii) Write an expression ... in Step y." (question starts at the foot of pdf page 33, the patterns are printed at the top of pdf page 34, printed page 11, left half)
description: Pattern (a): three steps printed side by side, left to right, labelled below each figure 'Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3'; a small caption '(a)' is printed below and centred under the group. Basic unit = one small square cell, pale yellow fill with thin dark outline, cells touching each other (no gaps), all the same size in all steps. Every step has the same Z / S shape: a solid rectangular block in the middle, one vertical column of cells hanging DOWN from the leftmost column of the block, and one vertical column of cells rising UP from the rightmost column of the block. The bottom edges of the three blocks are on the same level. Step n = a block (n+2) cells wide and n cells tall, plus n+2 cells stacked below the block's leftmost column, plus n+2 cells stacked above the block's rightmost column (the block's own end cells are not counted again). Step 1 (9 cells, counted): block 3 wide x 1 tall (3 cells in one row); below its left cell a column of 3 more cells; above its right cell a column of 3 more cells. So the left column is 4 cells tall in total and the right column 4 cells tall in total, joined by the single middle cell of the row: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9. Step 2 (16 cells, counted): block 4 wide x 2 tall (8 cells); 4 cells stacked below the left column of the block; 4 cells stacked above the right column of the block: 8 + 4 + 4 = 16. Step 3 (25 cells, counted): block 5 wide x 3 tall (15 cells); 5 cells stacked below the left column; 5 cells stacked above the right column: 15 + 5 + 5 = 25. The text 'Step y.' printed just above the figures is the last words of the question sentence, not a label of the figure. Printed answer: Step n total = (n+2)^2 (9, 16, 25, then 36).

belongs_to: Figure it Out (third set) Q11 pattern (b): same question as pattern (a) (draw the next figure, units in Step 10, expression for Step y) (printed pdf page 34, printed page 11, right half)
description: Pattern (b): three steps printed side by side, left to right, labelled below each figure 'Step 1', 'Step 2', 'Step 3'; a small caption '(b)' is printed below and centred under the group. Basic unit = one solid cyan-blue square (about #00AEEF), no outline, with a small white gap between neighbouring squares (squares do not touch). All squares the same size in all steps. The three figures are top-aligned (first rows on the same level) and each figure is left-aligned. Step n = a full (n+1) x (n+1) square array of squares, plus one extra row of n squares placed directly below it, flush with the LEFT edge (the last square position of that row is empty). Step 1 (5 squares, counted): 2 rows of 2 squares (4), then 1 square below on the left: 4 + 1 = 5. Step 2 (11 squares, counted): 3 rows of 3 squares (9), then 2 squares below on the left: 9 + 2 = 11. Step 3 (19 squares, counted): 4 rows of 4 squares (16), then 3 squares below on the left: 16 + 3 = 19. Printed answer: Step n total = (n+1)^2 + n (5, 11, 19, then 29).

belongs_to: Answer to Q11 (i)(a): "Then next figure" - Step 4 of pattern (a), total = (2 + 4)^2 = (6)^2 = 36 (printed pdf page 34, printed page 11, middle of the page, centred)
description: One figure, labelled 'Step 4' below it (the label sits under the figure, centred). Same style as Q11 pattern (a): touching pale-yellow square cells with thin dark outlines, same Z / S shape. Step 4 = block 6 cells wide x 4 cells tall (24 cells, counted: 4 rows of 6); below the block's leftmost column a vertical stack of 6 cells; above the block's rightmost column a vertical stack of 6 cells. Total 24 + 6 + 6 = 36 cells (counted: the top stack 6, the block 4 x 6, the bottom stack 6). The left column of the whole figure is therefore 10 cells tall (4 in the block + 6 hanging down) and the right column 10 cells tall (4 in the block + 6 rising up). The printed answer text above it reads 'Total = (2 + 4)^2 = (6)^2 = 36'.
